intent.raw_query: Iceland Northern Lights and hot springs, $3500 couple, January

experiences.name: Northern Lights Hunt from Reykjavik
experiences.description: Join a guided minibus tour departing from central Reykjavik to chase the aurora borealis. Expert guides use real-time forecasts to find the clearest skies, often heading toward the Reykjanes Peninsula or Þingvellir area. Includes hot chocolate and photography tips.
experiences.location: Departing from Reykjavik City Centre, Capital Region

experiences.name: Blue Lagoon Geothermal Spa
experiences.description: Soak in the iconic milky-blue geothermal waters of the Blue Lagoon, located just 20 minutes from Reykjavik and conveniently near Keflavik Airport. Enjoy silica mud masks, swim-up bars, and steam caves. Book the Comfort package for access to towels and a drink included in the entry.

experiences.name: Golden Circle Day Tour
experiences.description: Explore Iceland's most celebrated natural route covering Þingvellir National Park (a UNESCO World Heritage Site where tectonic plates meet), the erupting Strokkur geyser at Geysir, and the thundering Gullfoss waterfall. Easily accessible from Reykjavik, making it ideal for centrally located travellers.

experiences.name: Snorkeling or Diving in Silfra Fissure
experiences.description: Snorkel or dive between the North American and Eurasian tectonic plates in crystal-clear glacial water at Silfra, located within Þingvellir National Park — the same area as the Golden Circle. Visibility exceeds 100 metres in some of the world's purest water. Dry suits are provided. Combine with the Golden Circle for a full day.

experiences.name: Laugardalslaug Geothermal Pool & Local Food at Hlemmur Mathöll
experiences.description: Start your morning with a soak at Laugardalslaug, Reykjavik's largest public geothermal pool complex featuring hot pots, steam rooms, and a waterslide — a true local experience just 2 km from the city centre. Afterward, head to Hlemmur Mathöll food hall for an authentic Icelandic lunch featuring lamb soup, skyr desserts, and fresh seafood from local vendors.

trip_options.title: Budget Explorer - Iceland
trip_options.description: Save money without sacrificing the experience. Perfect for travelers who value authentic local experiences over luxury.

day_by_day.morning: Arrive at Keflavik International Airport at 06:10. Clear customs and collect luggage. Take the Flybus or a budget shuttle to Reykjavik BSI terminal, then arrange onward transport or rental car toward Siglufjörður. The drive north via Route 1 and Route 76 takes approximately 5-6 hours — enjoy the dramatic winter landscape along the way.
day_by_day.afternoon: Arrive in Siglufjörður mid-afternoon. Check in to Hotel Siglunes on Lækjargata 10. Rest briefly, then take a gentle walk along the harbour front to get oriented. Siglufjörður is a charming former herring fishing town nestled in a narrow fjord — explore the colourful wooden houses and quiet streets.
day_by_day.evening: Visit the famous Herring Era Museum (Síldarminjasafnið) if still open, or simply stroll the waterfront as darkness falls and watch for the northern lights over the fjord. The town's minimal light pollution makes it an excellent aurora-watching spot.

meals.breakfast: Grab a coffee and pastry at the airport or pack snacks for the road journey north to save money.
meals.lunch: Pick up groceries at a local supermarket (Krónan or Nettó) in Akureyri if passing through — stock up on bread, cheese, skyr, and fruit for budget meals throughout the trip.
meals.dinner: Prepare a simple self-catered meal at the hotel using groceries purchased en route. Alternatively, try Hannes Boy restaurant in Siglufjörður for affordable Icelandic fish dishes.

day_by_day.notes: The drive from Reykjavik to Siglufjörður in January requires caution — check road conditions at road.is before departing. Tunnel fees apply on Route 76. Dress in warm layers. Sunrise is very late in January (around 11:00) so the drive will be mostly in darkness or twilight.

day_by_day.morning: After a late sunrise around 11:00, visit the Herring Era Museum (Síldarminjasafnið) — one of Iceland's best regional museums, telling the story of the herring boom that shaped this town. Entry fee is modest. Explore all three buildings at a leisurely pace.
day_by_day.afternoon: Drive or walk to the nearby Héðinsfjörður valley, an abandoned fjord settlement accessible via a short tunnel from Siglufjörður. The eerie, deserted farmsteads surrounded by towering mountains and frozen terrain make for a hauntingly beautiful winter walk. Keep an eye out for Arctic foxes.
day_by_day.evening: Return to Siglufjörður before dark. Set up a northern lights watch from the harbour or the hillside above town. Download the Vedur aurora forecast app and the Icelandic Met Office app to track activity. Bring a thermos of hot chocolate.

meals.breakfast: Skyr with granola and coffee prepared at the hotel.
meals.lunch: Packed lunch of sandwiches and fruit eaten at Héðinsfjörður.
meals.dinner: Cook pasta with canned tomatoes and local lamb mince purchased from the supermarket — a warm, filling budget meal.

day_by_day.notes: January days are very short — only about 5 hours of usable daylight. Plan outdoor activities tightly between 11:00 and 16:00. Héðinsfjörður tunnel is free to use.

day_by_day.morning: Drive south along the scenic Tröllaskagi peninsula (Route 76 and Route 82) toward Hofsós. The mountain road offers spectacular views of snow-capped peaks and frozen fjords. Stop at viewpoints along the way for photography.
day_by_day.afternoon: Visit Hofsós Swimming Pool — one of Iceland's most scenic geothermal pools, perched on a cliff overlooking Skagafjörður fjord. Entry is very affordable (around 1,000 ISK). Soak in the warm water while gazing at the winter fjord landscape. Afterward, explore the small Icelandic Emigration Centre in Hofsós village.
day_by_day.evening: Drive back to Siglufjörður via Route 76. Stop at a dark hillside on the return journey for northern lights watching if the forecast is favourable. The rural roads around Tröllaskagi have virtually zero light pollution.

meals.breakfast: Oatmeal with honey and coffee at the hotel.
meals.lunch: Packed sandwiches eaten in the car or at Hofsós.
meals.dinner: Grilled fish with boiled potatoes and butter — purchase fresh or frozen fish from a local shop in Siglufjörður.

day_by_day.notes: Check road conditions carefully before driving Route 82 in winter — some sections can be icy or temporarily closed. The Hofsós pool may have limited winter hours; call ahead to confirm opening times.

day_by_day.morning: Drive east along Route 76 through the Tröllaskagi tunnels toward Ólafsfjörður and then continue to Akureyri, Iceland's second-largest city (approximately 1.5 hours from Siglufjörður). Arrive in Akureyri and explore the charming town centre, including the iconic Akureyrarkirkja church perched on the hill.
day_by_day.afternoon: Visit Lystigarðurinn, the northernmost botanical garden in the world — beautiful even in winter with snow-covered grounds. Then soak in the Akureyri Swimming Pool (Sundlaug Akureyrar), a large geothermal facility with multiple hot tubs and pools. Entry is budget-friendly at around 1,000 ISK.
day_by_day.evening: Explore Akureyri's small but lively town centre. Browse the shops on Hafnarstræti. Head back toward Siglufjörður before conditions deteriorate. Alternatively, if aurora forecast is strong, stay near Akureyri for a dark-sky aurora hunt.

meals.breakfast: Coffee and toast at the hotel before departing.
meals.lunch: Akureyri has a Bonus supermarket — grab budget supplies and eat a picnic-style lunch in the car or a park bench.
meals.dinner: Strikið restaurant in Akureyri offers affordable lunch specials that sometimes extend to early dinner, or try Bautinn for classic Icelandic comfort food at moderate prices. Alternatively, cook at the hotel.

day_by_day.notes: Akureyri is a great place to stock up on groceries at Bonus (Iceland's cheapest supermarket chain). Fill up the fuel tank here as petrol is slightly cheaper in larger towns.

day_by_day.morning: Drive east from Siglufjörður toward the Mývatn region (approximately 2 hours via Route 1 east from Akureyri). Arrive at Lake Mývatn, one of Iceland's most geologically active and visually stunning areas. Visit the Skútustaðagígar pseudo-craters — strange volcanic formations rising from the frozen lakeshore.
day_by_day.afternoon: Explore the dramatic Dimmuborgir lava field — a labyrinth of twisted black lava pillars and arches formed by an ancient lava lake. Walk the marked trails through this otherworldly landscape. Then visit Hverfjall, a massive tephra crater ring — you can walk around its base in winter.
day_by_day.evening: Soak in the Mývatn Nature Baths (Jarðböðin við Mývatn) — a geothermal lagoon similar to the Blue Lagoon but far less crowded and more affordable (around 5,500 ISK). The milky blue water steams in the cold air, and the remote location offers excellent northern lights viewing from the water.

meals.breakfast: Early breakfast at the hotel before the drive.
meals.lunch: Packed lunch eaten at Dimmuborgir.
meals.dinner: Gamli Bærinn restaurant near Mývatn serves hearty Icelandic soup and lamb dishes at reasonable prices. Alternatively, self-cater at the hotel on return.

day_by_day.notes: This is a long day with significant driving. Consider whether to make it a two-night trip to Mývatn or a day trip. The Mývatn Nature Baths are open until 22:00, making an evening soak with aurora viewing very feasible. Book in advance online for a small discount.

day_by_day.morning: If staying near Mývatn, visit Námaskarð geothermal area (Hverir) — a surreal landscape of bubbling mud pools, steaming fumaroles, and vivid orange and yellow sulphur deposits. Entry is free. The contrast of the steaming earth against snow is extraordinary in winter.
day_by_day.afternoon: Visit Krafla volcanic caldera and the Víti explosion crater — a circular lake inside a volcanic crater. The road to Krafla may be icy; check conditions. Explore the Leirhnjúkur lava field, still warm from geothermal activity beneath the surface.
day_by_day.evening: Drive back toward Siglufjörður (approximately 2 hours). Stop at a dark roadside location for northern lights watching if the KP index is favourable. The vast open landscapes of northern Iceland offer unobstructed 360-degree aurora views.

meals.breakfast: Skyr and fruit at accommodation.
meals.lunch: Packed lunch at Námaskarð — eat in the car to stay warm.
meals.dinner: Self-catered dinner at Hotel Siglunes using groceries — lamb stew or soup is ideal for a cold winter evening.

day_by_day.notes: Námaskarð and Krafla are free to visit. The sulphur smell at Hverir is strong but harmless. Wear sturdy waterproof boots as the ground can be muddy even in winter near the hot vents.

day_by_day.morning: Rest day in Siglufjörður. Sleep in and recover from the busy first week. Take a slow morning walk through the town, visiting the small local shops and the harbour. Look for the colourful fishing boats moored in the icy fjord.
day_by_day.afternoon: Hike up the hillside above Siglufjörður for panoramic views of the fjord and surrounding mountains. The terrain is steep and snowy — wear crampons or microspikes if available. The views from even a modest elevation are spectacular. Look for ptarmigan and other winter birds.
day_by_day.evening: Dedicated northern lights evening. Drive a few kilometres out of town to a dark spot and set up for aurora watching. Bring warm blankets, a thermos, and a tripod for long-exposure photography. The fjord reflects the aurora beautifully on calm nights.

meals.breakfast: Leisurely hotel breakfast — eggs, toast, and coffee.
meals.lunch: Soup and bread at a local café in Siglufjörður, or self-catered.
meals.dinner: Treat yourself to dinner at Hannes Boy — try the fish of the day or lamb soup. Budget around 3,000-4,000 ISK per person.

day_by_day.notes: January is statistically one of the best months for northern lights in Iceland due to long nights. Check the aurora forecast at en.vedur.is every evening. A KP index of 2 or above with clear skies is sufficient for visible aurora in northern Iceland.

day_by_day.morning: Drive west along Route 76 and Route 1 toward the Skagafjörður region. Visit Glaumbær turf farm museum — a beautifully preserved 18th-century turf farmhouse complex that offers a fascinating glimpse into traditional Icelandic rural life. Entry is affordable.
day_by_day.afternoon: Continue to Varmahlíð and explore the Skagafjörður valley. Visit the Víðimýrarkirkja turf church — one of Iceland's last remaining traditional turf churches, a National Monument. The surrounding snowy landscape makes it incredibly photogenic. Stop at the Skagafjörður Heritage Museum if time allows.
day_by_day.evening: Drive back to Siglufjörður via the scenic coastal route. Stop at Sauðárkrókur, the largest town in Skagafjörður, to pick up groceries at the local supermarket. Watch for northern lights on the return drive through the open valley.

meals.breakfast: Oatmeal and coffee at the hotel.
meals.lunch: Café at Glaumbær serves traditional Icelandic pancakes (pönnukökur) with cream and jam — an affordable and delicious local treat.
meals.dinner: Self-catered dinner at the hotel — purchase fresh bread and smoked lamb (hangikjöt) from the supermarket in Sauðárkrókur for an authentic Icelandic meal.

day_by_day.notes: Glaumbær and Víðimýrarkirkja may have reduced winter hours — check ahead. The drive through Skagafjörður valley is stunning with snow-covered mountains on both sides.

day_by_day.morning: Drive east from Siglufjörður toward the Eyjafjörður region. Visit Dalvík, a small fishing village with a charming local feel. Stop at the Byggðasafnið Hvoll folk museum to learn about local history and the famous 1934 earthquake that devastated the town.
day_by_day.afternoon: Continue to Hrísey island — take the short ferry from Árskógssandur (runs year-round, very affordable). Hrísey is known as the 'Pearl of Eyjafjörður' and is home to large populations of ptarmigan. Walk the marked trails across the small island and enjoy the peaceful winter atmosphere.
day_by_day.evening: Return by ferry and drive back toward Siglufjörður. The Eyjafjörður fjord is one of Iceland's longest and offers beautiful views of snow-covered mountains reflected in the dark water. Stop for aurora watching on the return journey.

meals.breakfast: Toast and skyr at the hotel.
meals.lunch: Pack a lunch to eat on Hrísey island — there are limited dining options on the island in winter.
meals.dinner: Self-catered warm soup at the hotel — vegetable and lamb soup with crusty bread.

day_by_day.notes: Check the Hrísey ferry schedule in advance as winter departures are limited. The island is very quiet in January — dress warmly as it can be exposed and windy. Ptarmigan are often seen right along the walking paths.

day_by_day.morning: Drive south from Siglufjörður toward the Vatnsnes peninsula (approximately 2 hours via Route 1 west). Visit Hvítserkur, a dramatic 15-metre basalt rock stack rising from the sea, resembling a rhinoceros or dragon. The surrounding beach and the contrast with the dark winter sea is spectacular.
day_by_day.afternoon: Continue around the Vatnsnes peninsula — this is one of Iceland's best places to spot harbour seals. Visit the Icelandic Seal Centre (Selasetur) in Hvammstangi to learn about Iceland's seal populations. The centre has free or low-cost entry in winter.
day_by_day.evening: Drive back north toward Siglufjörður. The long return drive offers excellent aurora-watching opportunities across the open Húnafjörður bay area, which has very dark skies. Stop at a safe roadside pullout if aurora activity is detected.

meals.breakfast: Early breakfast at the hotel before the long drive.
meals.lunch: Packed lunch eaten at Hvítserkur beach.
meals.dinner: Self-catered dinner at the hotel — pasta with pesto and canned fish, a simple budget staple.

day_by_day.notes: Hvítserkur is best visited around high tide for dramatic photos with water surrounding the rock. Check tide tables in advance. The Vatnsnes peninsula road is generally passable in winter but can be icy — drive carefully.

day_by_day.morning: Explore Siglufjörður more deeply. Visit the Folk Music Centre (Þjóðlagasetur) which celebrates Icelandic folk music traditions. Then walk to the old ski area above town — Siglufjörður has a small ski hill that may be operating in January, offering very affordable lift tickets compared to major resorts.
day_by_day.afternoon: Drive through the Strákagöng and Héðinsfjörður tunnels to explore the neighbouring fjords of Ólafsfjörður. Walk around this quiet fishing village and visit the small local swimming pool for a warm geothermal soak. The pool has a hot tub with views of the surrounding mountains.
day_by_day.evening: Return to Siglufjörður for a final evening aurora watch from the harbour. The fjord's calm waters can create stunning reflections of the northern lights on clear nights. This is one of the most magical possible settings for aurora viewing in Iceland.

meals.breakfast: Skyr parfait with granola and berries at the hotel.
meals.lunch: Local bakery or café in Ólafsfjörður for soup and bread.
meals.dinner: Celebratory dinner at Hannes Boy in Siglufjörður — try the catch of the day with local vegetables. Budget around 3,500-4,500 ISK.

day_by_day.notes: The Siglufjörður ski area (Skarðsdalur) is small and family-oriented with very reasonable lift pass prices — ideal for a budget traveller wanting a unique experience. Check if lifts are operating before making the trip up.

day_by_day.morning: Final full day — take a slow morning to pack and prepare for departure. Walk the full length of Siglufjörður's harbour one last time, taking in the atmosphere of this remote and beautiful fishing town. Visit any local shops for Icelandic souvenirs — look for locally made items rather than tourist shops for better value.
day_by_day.afternoon: Drive to a nearby hot spring or geothermal area for a final soak. The Hofsós pool is a beautiful option for a farewell dip, or explore any smaller natural hot pots in the region. The Tröllaskagi peninsula has several lesser-known geothermal spots worth seeking out.
day_by_day.evening: Return to Siglufjörður for a final northern lights vigil. Set an alarm for midnight and check the aurora forecast — January nights are long and the chances of seeing the aurora are high. Spend the last evening reflecting on the trip from the dark harbour.

meals.breakfast: Full cooked breakfast at the hotel — eggs, toast, and coffee.
meals.lunch: Use up remaining groceries for a packed lunch at the hot spring.
meals.dinner: Final self-catered dinner using remaining food supplies — skyr, bread, cheese, and smoked fish for a traditional Icelandic spread.

day_by_day.notes: Begin packing and organising for the return journey. Confirm departure transport arrangements — the drive from Siglufjörður to Keflavik Airport takes approximately 5-6 hours, so plan accordingly for the flight home.

day_by_day.morning: Wake early and check out of Hotel Siglunes. Begin the long drive south toward Keflavik International Airport via Route 76 and Route 1. The drive takes approximately 5-6 hours depending on road conditions. Enjoy the winter landscape one final time as you pass through the Tröllaskagi tunnels and along the Ring Road.
day_by_day.afternoon: Arrive in the Reykjavik/Keflavik area with time to spare. If the flight is in the evening, consider a brief stop at the Reykjanes Peninsula — visit the Bridge Between Continents (free) where you can walk between the Eurasian and North American tectonic plates, or see the Reykjanes lighthouse and dramatic coastal cliffs.
day_by_day.evening: Arrive at Keflavik International Airport with plenty of time before departure. Return the rental car if applicable. Enjoy a final Icelandic hot dog (pylsur) from a petrol station — a beloved Icelandic budget food tradition — before heading through security.

meals.breakfast: Quick breakfast at the hotel or packed food for the road.
meals.lunch: Petrol station or roadside stop along Route 1 — Icelandic petrol stations have surprisingly good and affordable hot food including soup and sandwiches.
meals.dinner: Airport meal or snacks purchased before security — budget around 2,000-3,000 ISK for airport food.

day_by_day.notes: Check road conditions at road.is before departing Siglufjörður — January can bring sudden weather changes. Allow extra time for the drive in case of slow conditions. The Bridge Between Continents on the Reykjanes Peninsula is free to visit and a memorable final stop. Duty-free at Keflavik Airport is one of the cheapest places to buy Icelandic spirits and chocolate as souvenirs.

trip_options.title: Classic Iceland Experience
trip_options.description: The sweet spot between comfort and value. Enjoy quality accommodations, diverse experiences, and good food.

Afterward, head to Hlemmur Mathöll food hall for an authentic Icelandic lunch featuring lamb soup, skyr desserts, and fresh seafood from local vendors.

day_by_day.morning: Arrive at Keflavik International Airport at 06:10. Clear customs and collect luggage. Take the Flybus or rent a car toward Reykjavik. Check into a transit guesthouse or use luggage storage to freshen up. Given the very early arrival and long drive ahead to Siglufjörður (~5 hours), rest briefly in Reykjavik before beginning the journey north.
day_by_day.afternoon: Begin the scenic drive north from Reykjavik toward Siglufjörður via Route 1 and the Héðinsfjörður tunnel. Stop at Borgarnes for a coffee and stretch break. Continue through the Westfjords-adjacent highlands, passing dramatic winter landscapes of snow-dusted lava fields and frozen rivers. Arrive in Siglufjörður by late afternoon and check into Hotel Siglunes on Lækjargata 10.
day_by_day.evening: Settle into Hotel Siglunes and take a short stroll along the quiet harbor of Siglufjörður to get oriented. The town is one of Iceland's most picturesque fishing villages, nestled between steep mountains and the fjord. Watch for the northern lights after dinner — Siglufjörður's remote location and minimal light pollution make it an excellent aurora-viewing spot.

meals.breakfast: Grab a pastry and coffee at a café near Keflavik Airport or the Flybus terminal before departing Reykjavik.
meals.lunch: Stop at Hyrnan Restaurant in Borgarnes — a reliable mid-range roadside spot offering Icelandic lamb soup and sandwiches (~2,500–3,500 ISK).
meals.dinner: Dine at Hannes Boy restaurant in Siglufjörður, a beloved local spot known for fresh fish dishes and hearty Icelandic fare (~3,500–5,500 ISK per person).

day_by_day.notes: The drive from Reykjavik to Siglufjörður is approximately 5 hours in good conditions, but January roads can be icy and slow. Check road conditions at road.is before departing. Dress in warm layers. Sunset in January is around 15:30–16:00, so the drive will be partly in darkness. Keep aurora alert apps active (e.g., Vedur.is) for the evening.

day_by_day.morning: After breakfast at the hotel, explore the Herring Era Museum (Síldarminjasafnið) in Siglufjörður — one of Iceland's finest regional museums, telling the story of the town's booming herring industry in the early 20th century. The museum complex spans several restored buildings along the harbor (~1,800 ISK entry).
day_by_day.afternoon: Lace up and take a winter walk along the Siglufjörður harbor trail, admiring the colorful wooden houses against the snow-covered mountain backdrop. If conditions allow, drive the short distance to the Héðinsfjörður viewpoint via the tunnel for sweeping fjord panoramas. Return to town and warm up with a hot chocolate at a local café.
day_by_day.evening: Head out after dinner for a self-guided northern lights watch from the harbor or the hillside above town. Siglufjörður's position deep in a fjord surrounded by dark mountains creates a natural amphitheater for aurora viewing. Bring a tripod if you have a camera.

meals.breakfast: Enjoy the hotel breakfast at Hotel Siglunes — typically includes skyr, bread, cold cuts, eggs, and coffee.
meals.lunch: Grab a light lunch at Kaffi Rauðka, a cozy café in Siglufjörður offering soups, sandwiches, and homemade cakes (~1,800–2,800 ISK).
meals.dinner: Return to Hannes Boy or try the hotel restaurant for a warm dinner of pan-fried Arctic char or lamb stew (~3,500–5,000 ISK).

day_by_day.notes: January days are very short in Siglufjörður — the sun barely clears the mountain ridges and daylight lasts only about 5 hours. Plan outdoor activities between 11:00 and 15:30. Aurora activity is best checked via the Icelandic Met Office forecast at en.vedur.is.

day_by_day.morning: Drive south along the Tröllaskagi Peninsula (about 45 minutes) to the town of Hofsós, home to one of Iceland's most dramatically situated geothermal pools — the Hofsós Swimming Pool, perched on a cliff edge overlooking the fjord. Soak in the infinity-style hot tubs with views of Skagafjörður (~900 ISK entry). A perfect hot springs experience in a non-touristy setting.
day_by_day.afternoon: Continue south to Sauðárkrókur, the largest town in the Skagafjörður region. Visit the Skagafjörður Heritage Museum (Byggðasafn Skagfirðinga) to learn about the region's Viking-age history and horse culture (~1,500 ISK). Browse the small town center and pick up any supplies needed.
day_by_day.evening: Return to Siglufjörður by early evening. After dinner, keep watch for the northern lights from the hotel or a dark spot near the fjord. Cloud cover permitting, January offers long aurora windows from around 17:00 to 08:00.

meals.breakfast: Hotel breakfast at Siglunes before departing.
meals.lunch: Eat at Kaffi Krókur in Sauðárkrókur — a welcoming local café with daily soup specials and open-faced sandwiches (~2,000–3,000 ISK).
meals.dinner: Pick up groceries in Sauðárkrókur (Krónan supermarket) for a self-catered dinner at the hotel to save budget, or dine at Hannes Boy in Siglufjörður (~3,500–5,000 ISK).

day_by_day.notes: The Hofsós pool is a hidden gem and far less crowded than the Blue Lagoon. Bring your own towel or rent one on-site (~500 ISK). Road conditions between Siglufjörður and Hofsós can be challenging in January — check road.is and allow extra travel time.

day_by_day.morning: Take a day trip east along the Ring Road toward Akureyri, Iceland's 'Capital of the North' (about 1.5 hours from Siglufjörður). Arrive in Akureyri and visit the iconic Akureyrarkirkja church perched on a hill above the town. Stroll the pedestrian shopping street, Hafnarstræti, and browse local boutiques and bookshops.
day_by_day.afternoon: Visit the Akureyri Botanical Garden (Lystigarðurinn) — even in winter the grounds are atmospheric and the greenhouse is open. Then head to the Akureyri Art Museum (Listasafnið á Akureyri) for contemporary Icelandic art (~1,000 ISK). Alternatively, soak at Sundlaug Akureyrar, the town's excellent geothermal pool complex with hot tubs and a waterslide (~1,000 ISK).
day_by_day.evening: Enjoy dinner in Akureyri before the drive back to Siglufjörður. Akureyri has the best dining options in North Iceland. Return to the hotel by 21:00 and check aurora forecasts for a late-night viewing session.

meals.breakfast: Hotel breakfast at Siglunes before departing.
meals.lunch: Eat at Bláa Kannan café in Akureyri — a charming historic café with soups, quiches, and excellent coffee (~2,500–3,500 ISK).
meals.dinner: Dine at Strikið restaurant in Akureyri, offering panoramic fjord views and quality Icelandic cuisine including lamb and fish (~4,500–7,000 ISK per person).

day_by_day.notes: Akureyri is a worthwhile day trip with significantly more amenities than Siglufjörður. The drive back in the dark requires caution — the mountain road between Akureyri and Siglufjörður via Ólafsfjörður can be icy. Consider the tunnel route for safety.

day_by_day.morning: Dedicate the morning to a slow, restorative start. Sleep in slightly, then enjoy a leisurely hotel breakfast. Take a short winter hike on the lower slopes above Siglufjörður — the town sits at the base of dramatic peaks and even a 30-minute walk uphill rewards with stunning fjord views. Dress in full winter gear.
day_by_day.afternoon: Drive to Ólafsfjörður (about 20 minutes through the tunnel) and explore this smaller neighboring fishing village. Visit the local swimming pool for a warm soak (~900 ISK). Walk along the harbor and observe the working fishing boats. The village has a quiet, authentic Icelandic character rarely seen by tourists.
day_by_day.evening: Return to Siglufjörður for a relaxed evening. This is a great night to try aurora photography — set up near the harbor with a dark sky behind the mountains. If clouds obscure the sky, enjoy a quiet evening at the hotel with a book and a glass of Icelandic craft beer.

meals.breakfast: Extended hotel breakfast at Siglunes.
meals.lunch: Self-catered lunch using groceries — make sandwiches with Icelandic skyr, smoked lamb (hangikjöt), and rye bread (rúgbrauð) from the local store.
meals.dinner: Dinner at Hannes Boy in Siglufjörður — try the fish of the day, typically fresh cod or haddock caught locally (~3,500–5,000 ISK).

day_by_day.notes: This is a deliberate rest and recharge day. The trip is long and the weather can be demanding. Pacing yourself mid-trip ensures you enjoy the second half fully. Check the aurora forecast — a KP index of 3 or higher is ideal for viewing at this latitude (66°N).

day_by_day.morning: Drive east from Siglufjörður toward the Mývatn region (approximately 2.5 hours via Akureyri). This is one of Iceland's most geologically active and visually stunning areas. Arrive at the Mývatn Nature Baths (Jarðböðin við Mývatn) — a less-crowded, more affordable alternative to the Blue Lagoon with equally impressive geothermal waters (~5,500 ISK). Soak in the silica-rich blue lagoon with views of the volcanic landscape.
day_by_day.afternoon: Explore the Mývatn area's volcanic wonders. Visit Hverfjall crater (a short walk to the rim), the Dimmuborgir lava formations (eerie lava pillars and arches), and the Skútustaðagígar pseudocraters along the lake shore. The landscape feels otherworldly, especially dusted with winter snow.
day_by_day.evening: Drive back toward Akureyri and overnight at a guesthouse in Akureyri, or make the full return to Siglufjörður (total driving ~5 hours for the day). If staying in Akureyri, watch for northern lights from the outskirts of town away from streetlights.

meals.breakfast: Hotel breakfast at Siglunes before departing.
meals.lunch: Eat at Gamli Bærinn restaurant near Mývatn — a rustic farmhouse restaurant serving traditional Icelandic lamb soup and rye bread baked in geothermal ground (~2,500–3,500 ISK).
meals.dinner: If returning to Siglufjörður, dine at the hotel restaurant. If staying in Akureyri, try Rub23 for excellent sushi and grilled fish (~4,500–6,500 ISK).

day_by_day.notes: Mývatn is a full-day excursion from Siglufjörður. Consider whether to overnight in Akureyri to break up the driving. The Nature Baths are open until 22:00, making an evening soak with potential aurora views above the steam a magical experience. Book the Nature Baths in advance online.

day_by_day.morning: Begin the long drive south from Siglufjörður (or Akureyri) toward Reykjavik, approximately 5–6 hours. This is a travel day, but the Ring Road south offers spectacular scenery. Stop at Glaumbær turf farm museum near Varmahlíð (open limited winter hours — check ahead) to see traditional Icelandic turf houses (~1,500 ISK).
day_by_day.afternoon: Continue south through the Holtavörðuheiði highland plateau and down into the Borgarfjörður region. Stop at Deildartunguhver, Europe's most powerful hot spring, near Reykholt — a dramatic, steaming geothermal vent that's free to visit and walk around. Also visit Hraunfossar and Barnafoss waterfalls nearby (free, 10-minute detour).
day_by_day.evening: Arrive in Reykjavik by early evening. Check into a mid-range guesthouse or hotel in central Reykjavik (e.g., Guesthouse Butterfly or similar, ~15,000–20,000 ISK/night). Explore the Laugavegur street area and enjoy dinner in the capital.

meals.breakfast: Hotel breakfast at Siglunes (or Akureyri guesthouse) before departing.
meals.lunch: Stop at a petrol station café (N1 or Orkan) along the Ring Road for a quick and affordable hot dog (pylsur) and coffee — an Icelandic institution (~500–800 ISK).
meals.dinner: Dine at Messinn in Reykjavik, famous for its cast-iron skillets of fresh Icelandic fish served with butter and herbs (~4,500–6,500 ISK per person).

day_by_day.notes: This is the longest driving day of the trip. Start early (by 08:00) to arrive in Reykjavik with daylight remaining. The Hraunfossar waterfalls are stunning even in winter and worth the short detour. Keep the car rental if you have one, as you'll need it for the Golden Circle tomorrow.

day_by_day.morning: Join the Golden Circle Day Tour departing from central Reykjavik. First stop: Þingvellir National Park, a UNESCO World Heritage Site where the North American and Eurasian tectonic plates meet and where Iceland's first parliament (Alþingi) was established in 930 AD. Walk the Almannagjá rift valley and admire the frozen Öxará River.
day_by_day.afternoon: Continue the Golden Circle to the Geysir Geothermal Area, home to Strokkur geyser which erupts every 5–10 minutes shooting boiling water 20–30 meters into the air. Then visit Gullfoss waterfall — one of Iceland's most powerful and dramatic cascades, partially frozen in January and utterly spectacular. The tour typically returns to Reykjavik by 18:00–19:00.
day_by_day.evening: Back in Reykjavik, explore the old harbor area (Grandi) and the Harpa Concert Hall. Check aurora forecasts — if conditions look promising, head to a dark spot on the Reykjanes Peninsula or Þingvellir for aurora viewing after dinner.

meals.breakfast: Grab breakfast at a Reykjavik bakery — Brauð & Co on Frakkastígur is excellent for fresh sourdough and pastries (~1,500–2,000 ISK).
meals.lunch: Lunch is typically included or available at the Geysir Center café on the Golden Circle tour — lamb soup and sandwiches (~2,500–3,500 ISK).
meals.dinner: Dine at Grillmarkaðurinn (The Grill Market) in Reykjavik for high-quality Icelandic ingredients cooked over lava stone (~5,500–8,000 ISK) or the more affordable Sægreifinn (Sea Baron) for lobster soup (~2,500 ISK).

day_by_day.notes: The Golden Circle tour is one of the available experiences and is best done as a guided tour in January due to road conditions and short daylight. Book in advance through Reykjavik Excursions or similar operators (~9,000–12,000 ISK per person). Dress in full winter gear — Gullfoss is extremely cold and windy.

day_by_day.morning: Start the morning with a soak at Laugardalslaug, Reykjavik's largest and most beloved public geothermal pool complex. Enjoy the main pool, hot tubs at varying temperatures, steam room, and waterslide. This is where locals come to relax and socialize — a genuine cultural experience (~1,100 ISK entry). Bring a towel or rent one on-site.
day_by_day.afternoon: After the pool, head to Hlemmur Mathöll (Hlemmur Food Hall) for lunch — a vibrant indoor food market in a converted bus terminal featuring diverse food stalls from sushi to Icelandic lamb burgers to vegan options. Browse the stalls and graze. Afterward, visit the National Museum of Iceland (Þjóðminjasafn Íslands) for a deep dive into Icelandic history from settlement to modern times (~2,500 ISK).
day_by_day.evening: Join a Northern Lights Hunt guided minibus tour departing from central Reykjavik. Expert guides use real-time aurora forecasts and cloud cover maps to chase the best viewing locations outside the city. Tours typically run 21:00–01:00 (~9,000–12,000 ISK per person). This is one of the best ways to maximize aurora chances.

meals.breakfast: Eat at the hotel or grab a quick breakfast at a nearby café before heading to Laugardalslaug.
meals.lunch: Graze at Hlemmur Mathöll food hall — budget ~2,500–4,000 ISK for a satisfying multi-stall lunch experience.
meals.dinner: Eat before the aurora tour at Noodle Station on Laugavegur — excellent Thai-style noodle soups, fast, affordable, and warming (~1,800–2,500 ISK).

day_by_day.notes: The Laugardalslaug + Hlemmur Mathöll combination is one of the listed available experiences and pairs perfectly as a morning-into-afternoon activity. Book the Northern Lights Hunt tour in advance — January is peak aurora season and tours fill up. Most operators offer a free repeat tour if aurora is not visible due to clouds.

day_by_day.morning: Drive to the Blue Lagoon Geothermal Spa, located about 45 minutes from Reykjavik near Grindavík on the Reykjanes Peninsula. Arrive for your pre-booked morning slot (book well in advance — the Blue Lagoon requires reservations). Enjoy the iconic milky-blue silica-rich geothermal waters, silica mud masks, and steam caves. The Comfort package (~14,000–16,000 ISK) includes towel, silica mask, and one drink.
day_by_day.afternoon: After the Blue Lagoon, explore the Reykjanes Peninsula. Drive to the Bridge Between Continents (Miðlína) — a small footbridge spanning the rift between the North American and Eurasian tectonic plates (free). Visit the Reykjanesviti lighthouse and the dramatic Gunnuhver hot spring mud pools nearby (free). The volcanic landscape here is raw and otherworldly.
day_by_day.evening: Return to Reykjavik by late afternoon. Spend the evening exploring the Laugavegur and Skólavörðustígur shopping and dining streets. Visit the iconic Hallgrímskirkja church (exterior free; tower elevator ~1,000 ISK) for panoramic city views at dusk.

meals.breakfast: Light breakfast at the hotel before departing — the Blue Lagoon is best visited on an empty stomach for comfort in the water.
meals.lunch: The Blue Lagoon has an in-water bar (included in some packages) for light snacks. Alternatively, eat at the LAVA Restaurant inside the Blue Lagoon for a splurge (~5,000–8,000 ISK) or pack a lunch to eat in the car.
meals.dinner: Dine at Snaps Bistro Bar in Reykjavik — a French-Icelandic bistro with excellent mussels, steak tartare, and fish dishes in a lively atmosphere (~4,500–7,000 ISK).

day_by_day.notes: The Blue Lagoon MUST be booked in advance online — walk-ins are not accepted. Book the earliest available slot (07:00 or 08:00) to enjoy it before crowds arrive. The silica mud mask is included in the Comfort package and is excellent for skin. Avoid submerging your hair as the silica can be drying.

day_by_day.morning: Take a guided Snorkeling or Diving in Silfra Fissure tour at Þingvellir National Park (about 45 minutes from Reykjavik). Snorkel between the North American and Eurasian tectonic plates in crystal-clear glacial water with visibility up to 100 meters. The water is a constant 2–4°C but dry suits keep you warm. Tours depart around 09:00 (~19,000–25,000 ISK for snorkeling, more for diving). No experience required for snorkeling.
day_by_day.afternoon: After the Silfra experience, warm up with hot chocolate provided by the tour operator. Spend the afternoon at leisure in Þingvellir National Park — walk the Almannagjá gorge trail and visit the Öxará River waterfall (Öxarárfoss). The park is hauntingly beautiful in winter with frost and snow.
day_by_day.evening: Return to Reykjavik. Visit the Settlement Exhibition (Landnámssýningin) — an underground museum built around a Viking longhouse excavated beneath the city center (~2,200 ISK). Afterward, enjoy a final evening stroll along the old harbor.

meals.breakfast: Early hotel breakfast before departing for Silfra — the tour requires you to avoid eating 2 hours before snorkeling.
meals.lunch: Pack a thermos of soup and sandwiches to eat at Þingvellir after the snorkeling tour — there are limited food options in the park in winter.
meals.dinner: Celebrate the Silfra experience at Fiskmarkaðurinn (The Fish Market) in Reykjavik — creative Icelandic-Asian fusion seafood in an elegant setting (~5,500–8,500 ISK).

day_by_day.notes: Silfra snorkeling is a bucket-list experience and one of the listed available activities. Book well in advance through DIVE.IS or Arctic Adventures. You must be a confident swimmer. Dry suits are provided and guides give full instruction. Remove contact lenses before snorkeling. The water temperature is extreme — the dry suit is essential and effective.

day_by_day.morning: Spend a relaxed final full morning in Reykjavik. Visit the Perlan Museum (Wonders of Iceland) — a stunning glass dome building with exhibits on glaciers, volcanoes, and the northern lights, plus a real indoor ice cave (~3,900 ISK). The rooftop observation deck offers 360° views over Reykjavik and the surrounding mountains.
day_by_day.afternoon: Explore the Grandi harbor district — visit the Whales of Iceland exhibition (life-size whale models, ~3,500 ISK) or the Marshall House contemporary art galleries (free). Browse the Kolaportið flea market if it's open (weekends only — check schedule). Pick up Icelandic souvenirs: wool lopapeysa sweaters, skyr, licorice, and sea salt.
day_by_day.evening: Final northern lights attempt — if the forecast is favorable (check en.vedur.is), drive 20–30 minutes out of Reykjavik to a dark location such as the Grótta lighthouse peninsula or the Reykjanes lava fields. Alternatively, join a final Northern Lights Hunt tour for a guided experience with the best chance of success.

meals.breakfast: Treat yourself to breakfast at Café Loki near Hallgrímskirkja — traditional Icelandic breakfast with rye bread, smoked lamb, and skyr (~2,000–3,000 ISK).
meals.lunch: Grab a classic Icelandic hot dog (pylsur) from Bæjarins Beztu Pylsur — the most famous hot dog stand in Iceland, a must-do (~500 ISK). Add a bowl of lobster soup from Sægreifinn nearby (~2,500 ISK).
meals.dinner: Farewell dinner at Apotek Kitchen & Bar in central Reykjavik — stylish setting in a historic pharmacy building, excellent cocktails and Icelandic lamb and seafood (~5,500–8,000 ISK).

day_by_day.notes: This is your last full day — balance sightseeing with souvenir shopping and relaxation. The Perlan Museum is excellent for understanding Iceland's natural phenomena in context. If you haven't seen the northern lights yet, tonight is your last chance — the aurora forecast and cloud cover will determine the best strategy.

day_by_day.morning: Final morning in Iceland. Pack and check out of your Reykjavik accommodation. If your flight departs in the afternoon, use the morning for any last activities: a final dip at a Reykjavik geothermal pool (Sundhöll Reykjavíkur in the city center is beautiful and historic, ~1,100 ISK), or a walk along the Seltjarnarnes peninsula for coastal views and potential seabird spotting.
day_by_day.afternoon: Drive to Keflavik International Airport (45 minutes from Reykjavik). Return the rental car if applicable. Allow at least 2.5 hours before departure for check-in, security, and duty-free shopping. Pick up last-minute Icelandic gifts at the airport duty-free: Brennivín schnapps, Icelandic chocolate, and Skyr products.
day_by_day.evening: Depart Iceland with memories of the northern lights, steaming hot springs, volcanic landscapes, and the unique tranquility of Siglufjörður. Safe travels!

meals.breakfast: Final hotel breakfast or grab pastries and coffee at Sandholt Bakery on Laugavegur — one of Reykjavik's best bakeries (~1,500–2,500 ISK).
meals.lunch: Eat at the airport — Keflavik Airport has several decent options including a branch of Icelandic Fish & Chips (~2,500–3,500 ISK) or grab a meal at the gate.
meals.dinner: In-flight meal or at destination.

day_by_day.notes: Confirm your flight departure time and factor in the 45-minute drive to Keflavik plus potential winter road delays. The airport duty-free is well-stocked and competitively priced for alcohol and Icelandic specialty foods. Leave time to browse. Lopapeysa wool sweaters are best purchased in Reykjavik shops rather than the airport for better prices and selection.

highlights: Mix of paid and free experiences

trip_options.title: Premium Iceland Escape
trip_options.description: Indulge in the best the destination has to offer. Premium flights, luxury hotels, and exclusive experiences.

experiences.name: Northern Lights Hunt from Reykjavik
experiences.description: Join a guided minibus tour departing from central Reykjavik to chase the aurora borealis. Expert guides use real-time forecasts to find the clearest skies, often heading toward the Reykjanes Peninsula or Þingvellir area. Includes hot chocolate and photography tips.
experiences.location: Departing from Reykjavik City Centre, Capital Region

experiences.name: Blue Lagoon Geothermal Spa
experiences.description: Soak in the iconic milky-blue geothermal waters of the Blue Lagoon, located just 20 minutes from Reykjavik and conveniently near Keflavik Airport. Enjoy silica mud masks, swim-up bars, and steam caves. Book the Comfort package for access to towels and a drink included in the entry.

experiences.name: Golden Circle Day Tour
experiences.description: Explore Iceland's most celebrated natural route covering Þingvellir National Park (a UNESCO World Heritage Site where tectonic plates meet), the erupting Strokkur geyser at Geysir, and the thundering Gullfoss waterfall. Easily accessible from Reykjavik, making it ideal for centrally located travellers.

experiences.name: Snorkeling or Diving in Silfra Fissure
experiences.description: Snorkel or dive between the North American and Eurasian tectonic plates in crystal-clear glacial water at Silfra, located within Þingvellir National Park — the same area as the Golden Circle. Visibility exceeds 100 metres in some of the world's purest water. Dry suits are provided. Combine with the Golden Circle for a full day.

experiences.name: Laugardalslaug Geothermal Pool & Local Food at Hlemmur Mathöll
experiences.description: Start your morning with a soak at Laugardalslaug, Reykjavik's largest public geothermal pool complex featuring hot pots, steam rooms, and a waterslide — a true local experience just 2 km from the city centre. Afterward, head to Hlemmur Mathöll food hall for an authentic Icelandic lunch featuring lamb soup, skyr desserts, and fresh seafood from local vendors.

day_by_day.morning: Arrive at Keflavík International Airport at 06:10 on Icelandair. Clear customs and collect luggage. Arrange private luxury transfer (pre-booked Mercedes V-Class or similar) from the airport. Given the early arrival and the long drive north to Siglufjörður (~5–6 hours), stop at the Blue Lagoon en route — doors open at 08:00. Soak in the iconic milky-blue geothermal waters, enjoy the in-water bar, and use the premium Retreat Spa facilities to refresh after the overnight flight.
day_by_day.afternoon: Depart Blue Lagoon around 11:30 and continue the scenic drive north via Route 1 (Ring Road). Stop in Borgarnes for a light lunch break. Continue through the Hvalfjörður tunnel and along the dramatic Snæfellsnes peninsula coastline views. Pass through Varmahlíð and wind through the stunning Héðinsfjörður mountain pass toward Siglufjörður. Arrive at Hotel Siglunes in the late afternoon, check in, and settle into your room overlooking the fjord.
day_by_day.evening: Enjoy a quiet first evening at Hotel Siglunes. Dine at the hotel's own restaurant, which serves locally sourced Icelandic cuisine including fresh Arctic char and lamb. After dinner, step outside to scan the sky for the northern lights — Siglufjörður's remote location and minimal light pollution make it an exceptional aurora-viewing spot.

meals.breakfast: Light refreshments at Blue Lagoon's Lava Restaurant (included with premium entry) — smoked salmon, skyr parfait, and Icelandic pastries
meals.lunch: Borgarnes Settlement Center Café — hearty Icelandic lamb soup and fresh bread during the road trip stop
meals.dinner: Hotel Siglunes Restaurant — pan-seared Arctic char with dill butter, roasted root vegetables, and Icelandic skyr dessert; pair with a local craft beer or Icelandic gin

day_by_day.notes: Pre-book the Blue Lagoon Retreat Spa package well in advance as slots fill quickly. Ensure the private transfer driver is briefed on the Blue Lagoon stop. The drive from Blue Lagoon to Siglufjörður is approximately 4.5–5 hours after the spa visit — plan to arrive before dark (sunset around 16:00 in January). Pack warm layers for the outdoor aurora viewing. Road conditions in January can be challenging; confirm Route 76 through Héðinsfjörður is open or use the Strákagöng tunnel alternative.

day_by_day.morning: Wake up to the dramatic winter scenery of Siglufjörður fjord. After a leisurely breakfast at the hotel, take a guided walk through the charming town of Siglufjörður — once the herring capital of the world. Visit the award-winning Herring Era Museum (Síldarminjasafnið), which offers a fascinating insight into Iceland's early 20th-century fishing boom. The museum is a short walk from the hotel.
day_by_day.afternoon: Hire a local guide for a snowshoe or winter hiking excursion into the mountains surrounding Siglufjörður. The terrain above the town offers breathtaking views of the fjord and surrounding peaks. Alternatively, arrange a private ice fishing experience on a nearby frozen lake with a local expert — a uniquely Icelandic winter activity. Return to the hotel for a warm-up with Icelandic hot chocolate and a sauna session.
day_by_day.evening: Northern lights hunt from Siglufjörður. The town's position deep in a fjord surrounded by mountains creates a natural amphitheater for aurora viewing. Bundle up and head to a pre-scouted dark-sky location just outside town with a local guide. Bring a thermos of hot cocoa and a tripod for photography. Return to the hotel for a late dinner.

meals.breakfast: Hotel Siglunes — full Icelandic breakfast with smoked lamb, skyr, fresh bread, eggs, and Icelandic dairy
meals.lunch: Café Rauðka in Siglufjörður — a cozy local café serving homemade soups, open-faced sandwiches, and Icelandic pastries
meals.dinner: Hotel Siglunes Restaurant — slow-braised Icelandic lamb shank with root vegetable purée, pickled red cabbage, and a rich lamb jus; finish with a warm skyr cake

day_by_day.notes: The Herring Era Museum may have limited winter hours — confirm opening times in advance. For the snowshoe hike, arrange equipment rental or hire through the hotel concierge. January aurora activity is strong in northern Iceland; the KP index forecast should be monitored via the Icelandic Met Office app (vedur.is). Dress in full thermal layers, waterproof outer shell, and insulated boots for all outdoor activities.

day_by_day.morning: After breakfast, take a private day excursion west along the Tröllaskagi peninsula toward Hofsós and Sauðárkrókur. Stop at the Hofsós Infinity Pool — a stunning geothermal swimming pool perched on a cliff edge overlooking Skagafjörður fjord. In winter, soaking in the warm geothermal water while surrounded by snow-capped mountains and fjord views is an extraordinary experience.
day_by_day.afternoon: Continue to Sauðárkrókur, the largest town in the Skagafjörður region. Visit the Skagafjörður Heritage Museum for insight into the region's Viking and medieval history. Explore the town briefly before heading to a local horse farm for a private Icelandic horse experience — these compact, spirited horses are unique to Iceland and riding or simply interacting with them in a snowy landscape is magical.
day_by_day.evening: Return to Siglufjörður in the late afternoon. Enjoy a relaxing evening at the hotel — use the sauna and hot tub facilities. Dine in and ask the hotel to arrange a special chef's tasting menu for the evening, showcasing the best of North Icelandic ingredients.

meals.breakfast: Hotel Siglunes — smoked salmon on rye, soft-boiled eggs, skyr with berries, and strong Icelandic coffee
meals.lunch: Kaffi Krókur in Sauðárkrókur — a well-regarded local restaurant serving fresh fish of the day, lamb burgers, and homemade soups
meals.dinner: Hotel Siglunes — chef's tasting menu: amuse-bouche of smoked trout mousse, pan-seared scallops, reindeer tenderloin with juniper berry sauce, and a skyr panna cotta with crowberry coulis

day_by_day.notes: Hofsós Pool is approximately 45 minutes from Siglufjörður — confirm winter opening hours as they can be limited. Bring a swimsuit and towel (or rent on-site). The Icelandic horse farm visit should be pre-arranged through the hotel concierge. Road conditions on the Tröllaskagi peninsula in January require a 4WD vehicle — ensure your rental or private driver has an appropriate vehicle. The chef's tasting menu at the hotel should be requested at least 24 hours in advance.

day_by_day.morning: Dedicate the morning to a private guided photography tour of Siglufjörður and its surroundings. A professional local photographer will guide you to the most photogenic winter spots — the colorful harbor, snow-laden rooftops, dramatic mountain reflections in the fjord, and the old herring factory ruins. This is an ideal way to capture the essence of this remote Arctic town.
day_by_day.afternoon: Drive through the Héðinsfjörður valley (or via the Strákagöng tunnel) to explore the neighboring fjord of Ólafsfjörður. This small fishing village has a charming character and is surrounded by dramatic peaks. Visit the local swimming pool (geothermal, naturally) for a warm soak, and explore the village on foot. The drive between the two fjords is itself spectacular in winter.
day_by_day.evening: Return to Siglufjörður for the evening. Tonight, arrange a private northern lights boat tour on the fjord — a unique way to experience the aurora away from any light pollution, with the reflections shimmering on the dark water below. A local skipper will take you out on a small heated vessel. Return to the hotel for a late dinner.

meals.breakfast: Hotel Siglunes — full hot breakfast with Icelandic oatmeal porridge, fresh pastries, cold cuts, and skyr
meals.lunch: Packed luxury picnic prepared by Hotel Siglunes — thermos of soup, smoked lamb sandwiches on rye, fruit, and Icelandic chocolate
meals.dinner: Hotel Siglunes — pan-fried cod with brown butter and capers, roasted fennel, and a warm chocolate lava cake with skyr ice cream

day_by_day.notes: The photography tour guide should be booked in advance — the hotel concierge can recommend local professionals. Bring extra camera batteries as cold temperatures drain them rapidly. The northern lights boat tour is weather and sea-condition dependent — have a backup plan (land-based aurora hunt) if conditions are unsuitable. Dress in extreme cold-weather gear for the boat excursion.

day_by_day.morning: Today, embark on a longer day trip east toward Akureyri — Iceland's 'Capital of the North' (approximately 1.5 hours from Siglufjörður via Route 82 and Route 1). Depart after breakfast and arrive in Akureyri mid-morning. Visit the iconic Akureyrarkirkja church perched on a hill above the town, then explore the charming pedestrian shopping street, Hafnarstræti.
day_by_day.afternoon: Visit the Akureyri Botanical Garden (Lystigarðurinn) — the world's northernmost botanical garden, beautiful even in winter with its snow-covered structures. Then head to the Akureyri Art Museum for a curated look at Icelandic contemporary art. In the late afternoon, indulge in a soak at the Sundlaug Akureyrar — the town's excellent geothermal pool complex with multiple hot pots and a stunning mountain backdrop.
day_by_day.evening: Dine at one of Akureyri's finest restaurants before the scenic drive back to Siglufjörður. The return journey along the fjord roads at night offers excellent aurora-viewing opportunities — keep your eyes on the sky.

meals.breakfast: Hotel Siglunes — full Icelandic breakfast before departure
meals.lunch: Rub23 Restaurant in Akureyri — one of the north's finest dining establishments, known for its creative sushi and Icelandic fusion cuisine; try the Arctic char sashimi
meals.dinner: Strikið Restaurant in Akureyri — rooftop restaurant with panoramic views; enjoy reindeer carpaccio, lobster bisque, and grilled lamb fillet before the drive back

day_by_day.notes: The drive from Siglufjörður to Akureyri takes approximately 1.5 hours in good conditions — allow extra time in January due to potential ice and snow. Check road conditions at road.is before departing. Akureyri's geothermal pool is open year-round and is a highlight — bring a swimsuit. Book dinner at Strikið in advance as it is popular. The return drive at night is beautiful but requires caution — a local driver is recommended.

day_by_day.morning: Take a private guided snowmobile tour in the mountains above Siglufjörður. The vast snowfields and mountain plateaus above the town are ideal for snowmobiling, offering exhilarating rides and panoramic views of the surrounding fjords and peaks. A certified local guide will lead the tour and provide all necessary equipment including helmets, suits, and gloves.
day_by_day.afternoon: Return to the hotel for lunch and a rest. In the afternoon, arrange a private visit to a local sheep farm to learn about traditional Icelandic farming practices in the Arctic winter. Many farms in the region welcome visitors and offer insight into how Icelanders have sustained themselves in this remote landscape for over a thousand years.
day_by_day.evening: Dedicated aurora evening. Tonight, work with a local aurora guide who monitors the KP index and cloud cover in real time to position you in the optimal location. Drive to a pre-scouted dark-sky spot in the mountains or along the fjord shore. Set up photography equipment and wait for the show. Hot drinks and snacks provided.

meals.breakfast: Hotel Siglunes — eggs Benedict with smoked salmon, fresh juice, and Icelandic coffee
meals.lunch: Hotel Siglunes — light lunch of lamb soup, fresh bread, and a green salad
meals.dinner: Hotel Siglunes — special request: traditional Icelandic lamb stew (kjötsúpa) followed by pan-seared halibut with lemon butter and asparagus, and a skyr cheesecake for dessert

day_by_day.notes: Snowmobile tours must be booked in advance through a certified operator — the hotel concierge can arrange this. Minimum age and weight restrictions may apply. The farm visit should also be pre-arranged. For the aurora evening, the Icelandic Met Office aurora forecast (en.vedur.is) is the most reliable source — aim for KP index 3 or above and clear skies. January in northern Iceland offers some of the best aurora probability in the country.

day_by_day.morning: Enjoy a slower morning. Sleep in and have a leisurely late breakfast at the hotel. Spend the morning in the hotel's wellness facilities — sauna, hot tub, and relaxation areas. Read, journal, or simply gaze out at the fjord from the warmth of the hotel lounge. This is a deliberate rest day built into the itinerary to recharge.
day_by_day.afternoon: Take a gentle self-guided walk along the Siglufjörður harbor front and into the old town. Visit the local craft and souvenir shops for authentic Icelandic woolens (lopapeysa sweaters), handmade ceramics, and local food products. Stop at a local bakery for fresh Icelandic pastries (kleinur or snúður). In the late afternoon, visit the Siglufjörður Folk Museum annex for additional local history.
day_by_day.evening: Arrange a private in-room or in-suite dining experience at Hotel Siglunes — a romantic and exclusive dinner served in your room or a private dining space, with a curated menu and wine pairing prepared by the hotel chef. Afterward, step outside for a final aurora check before retiring.

meals.breakfast: Hotel Siglunes — extended brunch: smoked fish platter, fresh pastries, skyr with honey and granola, eggs to order, and specialty coffee
meals.lunch: Local Siglufjörður bakery — fresh kleinur (Icelandic doughnuts), cinnamon snúður, and a bowl of fish soup
meals.dinner: Private in-room dining at Hotel Siglunes — five-course tasting menu with wine pairing: oysters, smoked lamb tartare, Arctic char with caviar, reindeer loin, and a dark chocolate and crowberry dessert

day_by_day.notes: The private dining experience should be arranged with the hotel at least 48 hours in advance. This rest day is intentionally low-key — the trip involves significant driving and outdoor activity in cold conditions, and recovery time is important for a premium experience. Use the afternoon shopping time to pick up authentic Icelandic gifts and souvenirs.

day_by_day.morning: Embark on a full-day private excursion to the Mývatn region (approximately 2.5 hours east of Siglufjörður via Route 1). Depart early after breakfast. Mývatn is one of Iceland's most geologically active and visually stunning areas. Begin with a visit to the Námaskarð geothermal area (Hverir) — a surreal landscape of bubbling mud pools, steaming fumaroles, and sulfurous vents set against vivid orange and yellow earth.
day_by_day.afternoon: Continue to the Mývatn Nature Baths — often called the 'Blue Lagoon of the North,' these geothermal pools offer a more intimate and less crowded experience than their famous southern counterpart. Soak in the mineral-rich, silica-blue water surrounded by volcanic landscapes and steam rising into the Arctic air. Afterward, visit the Dimmuborgir lava formations — an otherworldly landscape of twisted lava pillars and arches.
day_by_day.evening: Drive back toward Siglufjörður, stopping to scan for the northern lights along the way. The Mývatn area and the roads back through the highlands offer exceptional dark-sky conditions. Arrive back at the hotel for a late dinner.

meals.breakfast: Hotel Siglunes — full hot breakfast before the early departure
meals.lunch: Vogafjós Farm Restaurant at Mývatn — a unique farm-to-table experience where you can watch cows being milked through a glass window while dining; try the fresh mozzarella, smoked trout, and homemade bread
meals.dinner: Hotel Siglunes — late dinner of pan-seared lamb chops with rosemary jus, roasted potatoes, and a warm apple and skyr tart

day_by_day.notes: The Mývatn Nature Baths are open year-round and are significantly less crowded than the Blue Lagoon — book in advance for the premium lounge package. Bring a swimsuit and towel. The Námaskarð area is accessible in winter but can be icy — wear sturdy boots. The round trip from Siglufjörður to Mývatn is approximately 5 hours of driving — a private driver is strongly recommended. Depart by 08:00 to maximize daylight hours (approximately 5–6 hours of usable light in January).

day_by_day.morning: Today, drive south toward Reykjavik for the second half of the trip (approximately 5–6 hours). Depart after breakfast and take the scenic Route 1 south through the interior highlands. Stop at Goðafoss — the 'Waterfall of the Gods' — one of Iceland's most spectacular waterfalls, particularly dramatic in winter when partially frozen and surrounded by snow and ice.
day_by_day.afternoon: Continue south through Akureyri and along the Ring Road. Stop at Varmahlíð for a brief break and to admire the Skagafjörður landscape. Continue south through the Holtavörðuheiði highland plateau. Arrive in Reykjavik in the late afternoon. Check into your luxury Reykjavik accommodation (upgrade to a premium city hotel such as The Retreat at Blue Lagoon, Hotel Borg, or ION Adventure Hotel — pre-book separately).
day_by_day.evening: Freshen up and head out for dinner in Reykjavik's vibrant restaurant scene. Explore the Laugavegur area and enjoy the city's cosmopolitan energy after the remote tranquility of Siglufjörður.

meals.breakfast: Hotel Siglunes — final breakfast: smoked salmon, rye bread, skyr, and Icelandic coffee before checkout
meals.lunch: Packed luxury picnic from Hotel Siglunes for the road — thermos of soup, sandwiches, fruit, and Icelandic chocolate; enjoy at the Goðafoss viewpoint
meals.dinner: Dill Restaurant in Reykjavik — Iceland's first Michelin-starred restaurant; a Nordic tasting menu showcasing hyper-local Icelandic ingredients with creative, seasonal preparations; book well in advance

day_by_day.notes: Check out of Hotel Siglunes and ensure all luggage is packed the night before for an efficient morning departure. The drive to Reykjavik is long — a private driver is recommended. Goðafoss is accessible year-round but the paths can be icy in January — wear crampons or ice grips. Confirm your Reykjavik hotel booking well in advance. Dill Restaurant requires reservations months ahead — book before the trip.

day_by_day.morning: Start the day with a soak at Laugardalslaug — Reykjavik's largest and most beloved public geothermal pool complex. Arrive early (opens at 06:30 on weekdays) to enjoy the multiple hot pots, steam rooms, and outdoor pools before the crowds arrive. This is a quintessential local Reykjavik experience. Afterward, visit Hlemmur Mathöll — Reykjavik's premier food hall — for a gourmet breakfast featuring the best of Icelandic artisan food producers.
day_by_day.afternoon: Join the Golden Circle Day Tour — Iceland's most celebrated natural route. Visit Þingvellir National Park (UNESCO World Heritage Site), where the North American and Eurasian tectonic plates meet and Iceland's ancient parliament was founded. Continue to the Geysir geothermal area to witness Strokkur erupting every 5–10 minutes. Conclude at the majestic Gullfoss waterfall, partially frozen and thundering in January.
day_by_day.evening: Return to Reykjavik in the early evening. Freshen up at the hotel and head out for a Northern Lights Hunt from Reykjavik — join a guided minibus tour with expert aurora guides who monitor conditions in real time and drive to the best viewing locations outside the city. Return to the hotel after the hunt.

meals.breakfast: Hlemmur Mathöll food hall — artisan sourdough with smoked lamb, fresh pastries, specialty coffee, and Icelandic dairy products
meals.lunch: Friðheimar Greenhouse Restaurant (on the Golden Circle route) — a unique dining experience inside a working tomato greenhouse; tomato soup, tomato bruschetta, and fresh salads made entirely from greenhouse-grown produce
meals.dinner: Grillið Restaurant at Radisson Blu Saga Hotel — rooftop fine dining with panoramic Reykjavik views; Icelandic beef tenderloin, langoustine bisque, and a skyr soufflé

day_by_day.notes: Laugardalslaug opens at 06:30 on weekdays — arrive early for the best experience. Bring a swimsuit and towel (or rent on-site). The Golden Circle tour is approximately 8 hours — wear warm, waterproof layers. Friðheimar requires advance booking even in winter. The Northern Lights Hunt departs from central Reykjavik — book through a reputable operator such as Reykjavik Excursions or Arctic Adventures. Aurora success depends on weather and solar activity.

day_by_day.morning: Today, experience one of Iceland's most extraordinary adventures — snorkeling or diving in the Silfra Fissure at Þingvellir National Park. Silfra is the only place in the world where you can snorkel or dive directly between two tectonic plates in water of exceptional clarity (visibility up to 100 meters). The water temperature is 2–4°C year-round, but dry suits keep you warm. A certified guide will lead the experience.
day_by_day.afternoon: Return to Reykjavik and spend the afternoon exploring the city's cultural highlights. Visit the Hallgrímskirkja church and take the elevator to the top for panoramic city views. Explore the National Museum of Iceland for a deep dive into Icelandic history and culture. Browse the boutiques and design shops along Laugavegur for premium Icelandic design, fashion, and crafts.
day_by_day.evening: Enjoy a premium spa evening at the Sky Lagoon — Reykjavik's newest and most luxurious geothermal lagoon, featuring an infinity edge overlooking the North Atlantic Ocean. The Skjól ritual package includes access to the lagoon, sauna, cold plunge, steam room, and body scrub. Afterward, dine at the on-site Smakk Bar for a curated Icelandic tasting experience.

meals.breakfast: Hotel breakfast — full spread before the early departure for Silfra
meals.lunch: Café in Þingvellir National Park visitor center — warm soup and sandwiches after the snorkeling experience
meals.dinner: Smakk Bar at Sky Lagoon — Icelandic tasting platters featuring smoked lamb, skyr, dried fish, rye bread, and local cheeses, paired with Icelandic craft beers and spirits

day_by_day.notes: Silfra snorkeling requires advance booking — choose a reputable operator such as DIVE.IS or Arctic Adventures. Participants must be comfortable in water; no diving certification is required for snorkeling. Dry suits are provided but must fit properly — inform the operator of your measurements in advance. The water is extremely cold — follow all guide instructions. Sky Lagoon's Skjól package must be booked in advance online. The lagoon is open until 23:00, making it ideal for an evening visit.

day_by_day.morning: Dedicate the morning to a private guided tour of Reykjavik's most iconic landmarks and hidden gems. A knowledgeable local guide will take you through the old harbor area, the Harpa Concert Hall (a stunning glass structure on the waterfront), the colorful old town streets, and the Tjörnin lake. Visit the Reykjavik Art Museum's Hafnarhús branch for contemporary Icelandic art.
day_by_day.afternoon: Drive approximately 45 minutes to the Reykjanes Peninsula for a visit to the Gunnuhver hot spring area and the Bridge Between Continents — a small footbridge spanning the Mid-Atlantic Ridge. Explore the dramatic volcanic landscape of the peninsula, including the Krýsuvík geothermal area with its steaming vents and colorful mineral deposits. Return to Reykjavik in the late afternoon.
day_by_day.evening: Final northern lights attempt — tonight, arrange a premium private northern lights tour with a dedicated photographer-guide who will help you capture the aurora on camera. Drive to the darkest available location based on real-time cloud cover forecasts. This is your last opportunity for aurora viewing — make it count. Return to Reykjavik for a celebratory farewell dinner.

meals.breakfast: Hotel — leisurely breakfast with smoked fish, fresh pastries, eggs, and specialty coffee
meals.lunch: Pakkhús Restaurant in Reykjavik harbor area — fresh Icelandic seafood; try the langoustine tails, fish and chips with Icelandic malt vinegar, and a bowl of lobster soup
meals.dinner: Óx Restaurant in Reykjavik — an ultra-exclusive, reservation-only counter-dining experience with only 12 seats; a theatrical multi-course tasting menu celebrating Icelandic ingredients at their finest; book months in advance

day_by_day.notes: The private city tour guide should be booked in advance — the hotel concierge can recommend excellent options. The Reykjanes Peninsula roads are generally well-maintained but can be icy in January — a 4WD vehicle is advisable. Óx Restaurant is one of the hardest reservations to secure in Iceland — book as early as possible, ideally when planning the trip. If unavailable, alternatives include Matur og Drykkur or Fiskfélagið (Fish Company). The private aurora tour should be booked with a photographer-guide who provides post-processing of your images.

day_by_day.morning: Final morning in Iceland. Depending on your departure flight time, enjoy a last leisurely breakfast at the hotel. Take a final walk along Reykjavik's harbor front to breathe in the Arctic air and reflect on the journey. If time permits, visit the Kolaportið flea market (open weekends only — check if applicable) or do any last-minute shopping on Laugavegur for Icelandic woolens, lava salt, skyr products, and local spirits.
day_by_day.afternoon: Check out of the hotel and arrange a private luxury transfer to Keflavík International Airport (approximately 45 minutes from central Reykjavik). If your flight departs in the afternoon or evening, consider a final stop at the Blue Lagoon for a farewell soak — the airport is only 20 minutes from the lagoon, making it a perfect last Icelandic experience. Depart Iceland with extraordinary memories.
day_by_day.evening: Departure from Keflavík International Airport. Enjoy the Icelandair Saga Lounge before boarding for a premium pre-flight experience with Icelandic food and drinks.

meals.breakfast: Hotel — final Icelandic breakfast: skyr with blueberries, smoked salmon on rye, fresh pastries, and strong coffee
meals.lunch: Blue Lagoon Lava Restaurant (if stopping for a final soak) — smoked lamb flatbread, Icelandic fish soup, and a glass of sparkling wine as a farewell toast
meals.dinner: Icelandair Saga Lounge at Keflavík Airport — Icelandic snacks, open bar, and light bites before departure

day_by_day.notes: Confirm your departure flight time and work backward to plan the morning. Allow at least 2.5–3 hours before departure for airport check-in and security. If doing a final Blue Lagoon visit, book the Premium or Retreat package in advance and allow at least 2 hours for the experience plus travel to the airport. Ensure all luggage is packed and hotel checkout is completed efficiently. Keep a small bag accessible for the Blue Lagoon visit with swimsuit and essentials. The Saga Lounge is available to Saga Class passengers and Saga Club Gold/Silver members.
